note:
Trajectory and energy data as PUBLISHED BY THE MANUFACTURER, transcribed unchanged. SPEC.md §8.3 requires the solver be checked against published tables as well as against an independent implementation, and this is that half. Nothing here is computed by us: every number in `rows` is printed on the cited page. Facts are not copyrightable; we transcribe the figures and never republish the page.

What each table can and cannot validate:
  - The energy column is a closed-form function of the velocity column and the bullet mass, with no free parameters, so `ballistics/energy` is checked against it EXACTLY (to the rounding the manufacturer publishes at).
  - The trajectory column needs a ballistic coefficient, which Hornady does not publish on these pages. Rather than borrow a BC from elsewhere and pretend it is theirs, the test FITS a G1 BC to the published velocity column and then checks the published drop — which is a real test of the integrator, because drop comes from time of flight and gravity and is not what the fit was tuned on.
